## Lower support determines the canonical word

For arbitrary positive raw matrix words the following monomials have strictly
positive coefficients. Write B-count as c and word length as l:

* In x r y: u^(c(y)) v^(l(x)+indicator(r=B)).
* In A x r y B: u^(c(x)+1) v^(l(y)+2).

The first path stays in the upper matrix state, exits at r, then stays in
the lower state. The second exits at the initial A, returns at r, and exits
again at the final B. MarkovWordWitness28b1 proves positivity directly from
the exact raw generators and coefficient convolution, not by tropical tests.

# Exact support, mechanical words, and strategy obstructions

Machine-authored request 3edac4bf4f1040d0b967711f6c52c66f. Validation status is
recorded by source hash in evidence/markov-3edac4bf/validation.json. None of
these results proves or refutes the full pinned Conjecture63.

## Saturation from exact prefix counts

Write a,b for a source middle label and W for its raw A/B word, of length b
with a copies of B. The inherited support-rigidity proof identified proper
central prefix counts. MarkovMechanical3eda extends this to the entire word:

    count_B(take j W) = floor(a*j/b),    0 <= j <= b.

The j=0,b-1,b endpoint cases are explicitly checked, using 0<a<b. The exact
raw-word/source polynomial identity is also recorded, without normalization.

For 0<j<b, split W=x r y with length(x)=j-1. The inherited positive matrix
path witness gives a positive coefficient at

    (count_B(y), length(x)+indicator(r=B)).

Its second coordinate is at most j. If q=count_B(take j W), then a=q+count_B(y)
and a*j < b*(q+1). At any polygon point (i,j), the inequality
a*b <= b*i+a*j therefore forces count_B(y)<=i. The inherited northeast
support propagation reaches (i,j), since i+j<=a+b-1. For j=0 use the positive
vertex (a,0); for j>=b use (0,b). This proves source_saturated3eda for every
finite path and every polygon lattice point, with no bound on a or b.

Combining it with the existing outside-zero theorem gives exactly

    0 < A_ij iff InPolygon(a,b,i,j),
    A_ij = 0 iff not InPolygon(a,b,i,j).

This is stronger than convex-hull equality or interval support: every polygon
lattice point has a nonzero raw coefficient. It does not compare coefficient
magnitudes. Saturation is already a known mathematical result; the primary
paper [Evans, Saturation of Markov Polynomials](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.18333v1)
was retrieved live. This run uses a checked matrix-word argument, not an external
theorem as an axiom, and makes no historical novelty claim.

## An explicit arithmetic root formulation

Define the length-b word by its kth letter:

    W(a,b)[k] = B if floor(a*k/b) < floor(a*(k+1)/b), else A.

MarkovMechanicalGoal3eda proves exact equality with each source word by taking
successive prefix-count differences. Conversely rational_coverage_098 supplies
an actual source path for every positive reduced a<b, with literal polynomial
equality to the raw matrix product of W(a,b).

root_iff_mechanical3eda equates the full pinned root with GlobalLC18 for all
these explicit words. There is no support condition or unknown family bridge
on this new target. Both sides remain unproved. The equivalence retains the
three raw directions, all indices and zeros, and uses the inherited vacuous
0/1 and 1/1 endpoint clauses through root_iff_raw_matrix18.

## All diagonal support and cross inequalities

For every n define D_n(k)=A_{k,n-k} when 0<=k<=n, and zero otherwise. Saturation
and the linear polygon inequalities give interval support for every D_n,
including lower diagonals. Together with nonnegativity, the inherited adjacent
to CrossLC theorem applies without a no-gap premise. MarkovCrossGoal3eda glues
this to the analogous horizontal and vertical results into a full-root
equivalence with CrossLC on every raw slice. Neither inequality side is proved.
This concerns raw slices; it does not claim log-concavity of quotient slices
or invert the smoothing transform.

## Obstructions explored and checked

1. The gas core ACAAAAACA is a balanced palindrome. Its raw scalar polynomial
has vertical coefficients 8,12,20 at (1,5),(1,6),(1,7), hence 144<160. Lean
checks both structural properties and the failure of GlobalLC18. The coefficient
at (1,5) violates the lower polygon bound for 3/8 (23<24), so the polynomial
cannot be that source. This is not a source-family counterexample. The short
enumerations and full words are in palindrome-scan.json and balanced-palindrome.json.

2. An exact source scan through b=35 tests primitive directions with components
bounded by 4, retaining polygon guards and zeros. It checks 3,445,704 triples
on 383 sources. It finds failures in additional directions; the three pinned
directions have no failure in this finite test. At 1/9, the direction (1,-3)
has coefficients 1,7,50 at (0,9),(1,6),(2,3), so 49<50. All three points are
inside the source polygon. MarkovDirectionObstruction3eda checks the exact
source recurrence coefficients, labels, polygon memberships and reversed
inequality. This excludes full arbitrary-direction concavity, not the pinned
weak concavity. The exact scan is directions-probe.json.

These are strategy exclusions, not root refutations. The [published target](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html)
specifies only (1,0),(0,1),(1,-1); no failed additional direction is silently
included in its meaning.

# Source symmetry and polygon rigidity

Machine-authored research for request 28b112de527c4d3ea1fa665cec2dc394.
Full pinned Conjecture63 remains unresolved. Acceptance status for each Lean
module is recorded in evidence/markov-28b112de/validation.json; a draft or
rejected elaboration is not a theorem.

## Palindrome and positive squares

Let W be the exact A/B source word. The two word substitutions are
L(A)=A,L(B)=AB and R(A)=AB,R(B)=B. Naturality with the actual Farey pair
recursion proves W=A c B where c is the recursively defined central word.
If c is a palindrome, L(c)A and B R(c) are palindromes; induction proves this
for every finite source path. Expanding B to AC gives the exact gas core
L(c)A, again a palindrome. This is an exact source-word assertion, stronger
than merely exhibiting an unspecified word with the right counts.

For a gas word w with matrix M, define

    Q_w(x,y)=v*x²*M.a+u*v*x*y*M.b+x*y*M.c+u*y²*M.d.

Sandwiching w by the same letter transforms its boundary pair by

    h=v*x+u*y,
    (x,y) -> (h+t*x,h) for C, or (h,h+t*y) for A.

The empty core has Q=v*x²+u*y². A singleton has
Q=(v*x+u*y)²+t*v*x² for C, or Q=(v*x+u*y)²+t*u*y² for A.
These are polynomial identities over arbitrary commutative rings.
At t=1, palindrome induction and nonnegativity of all boundary updates prove
that every actual source raw numerator has one of these three forms:

    v*f²+u*g²,  f²+u*g²,  f²+v*g²,

where f,g are bivariate integer polynomials with nonnegative coefficients.
MarkovSquares28b1.source_positive_squares28 states exactly this existential
result. No log-concavity closure under addition or squaring is invoked.

The exact Python check agrees with all 627 source polynomials through b=45.
It also finds that the canonical half polynomial f can fail raw vertical LC:
at source 3/44 it has [12,14,18], so 196<216. This is an experimental
obstruction to requiring LC of every half factor; it is not a counterexample
to the source numerator, and this obstruction has not been formalized in Lean.

## Lower support determines the canonical word

For arbitrary positive raw matrix words the following monomials have strictly
positive coefficients. Write B-count as c and word length as l:

* In x r y: u^(c(y)) v^(l(x)+indicator(r=B)).
* In A x r y B: u^(c(x)+1) v^(l(y)+2).

The first path stays in the upper matrix state, exits at r, then stays in
the lower state. The second exits at the initial A, returns at r, and exits
again at the final B. MarkovWordWitness28b1 proves positivity directly from
the exact raw generators and coefficient convolution, not by tropical tests.

Let w=A x r y B have a B letters and length b, with 0<a<b and gcd(a,b)=1.
Suppose every positive coefficient satisfies a*b<=b*i+a*j. Put k=c(x),
l=l(x)+1. The suffix witness yields b*k<=a*l; the prefix-loop witness yields
a*l<=b*(k+1). Equality in the latter would force b|l by coprimality, impossible
for 0<l<b. Therefore k=floor(a*l/b). All proper prefix counts are forced.
The full core count is a-1, which also determines its final letter.

MarkovPolygonWord28b1 formalizes the floor constraint. MarkovWordRigidity28b1
uses equality of all prefix counts to prove uniqueness of a supported core.
Combining this with the inherited exact rational-coverage theorem identifies
every such reduced A--core--B word with an actual source path and its literal
raw numerator. Consult validation for completed versus draft status.

MarkovSupportedGoal28b1 states an exact equivalence between the pinned root
and raw GlobalLC for every reduced A--core--B word satisfying the lower
polygon support constraint. The forward direction uses the new source-word
characterization. The reverse uses each source's actual canonical word and
the inherited endpoint and outside-polygon-zero bridges. All three directions,
all natural coefficient indices and zeros remain present. Neither side of this
equivalence is proved; no extra support-to-LC assertion is silently introduced.

The tropical scan through b=23 tests 3,056,949 reduced A--core--B words and
finds exactly 171 supported words, one per reduced interior label, always the
lower mechanical word. This is finite evidence; the Lean argument instead
uses the two universal monomial witnesses. The scan's costs are minimum
b*i+a*j in the positive matrices, not new polynomial normalizations.

## Consequences and limits

These results provide global structural descriptions of the exact source
family. They do not establish any new universal interior log-concavity
inequality, and in particular do not prove that positive squares or polygon
containment imply LC for arbitrary polynomials. The supported-word theorem
restricts to the precise two raw generators, endpoints A/B and coprime counts.
Removing those hypotheses is not justified.

The previous worker's sixth-diagonal proof was already complete. Its attempted
second-horizontal-row argument duplicated MarkovSecondHorizontal8934, which
had already proved that result. The present run preserves both histories and
abandons the duplicate instead of claiming it as new progress.

def expand80 : List Bool → List Bool
  | [] => []
  | false::rs => false::expand80 rs
  | true::rs => false::true::expand80 rs

theorem expand_append80 (x y : List Bool) : expand80 (x++y)=expand80 x++expand80 y := by
  induction x with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons r rs ih => cases r <;> simp [expand80,ih]

def rawWord80 : List Bool → Mat16 BiPoly
  | [] => ⟨1,0,0,1⟩
  | r::rs => mm16 (if r then rawB18 else rawA18) (rawWord80 rs)

theorem rawWord_append80 (x y : List Bool) :
    rawWord80 (x++y)=mm16 (rawWord80 x) (rawWord80 y) := by
  induction x with

    · simp only [rawWord80,if_true,expand80,gasWord80,rawB_factor80,ih,mm_assoc16]

# Pell matching formula and all diagonal inequalities

Machine-authored request 061840e8bcb9466891906a9db3f46cc3. The authoritative
local build/replay statuses are hash-bound in evidence/markov-061840e8/validation.json.
Full pinned Conjecture63 remains unresolved. No historical novelty claim is made.

Define E_0=P_0=1 and

    P_(n+1)=E_n+u P_n,
    E_(n+1)=P_(n+1)+v E_n.

These are the matching polynomials of alternating-edge paths (the graph
interpretation is explanatory; the formal definition is the positive recurrence).
Induction using Pascal's identity proves, for every n,i,j in the natural numbers,

    [u^i v^j] E_n = choose(n-j,i) choose(n-i,j),
    [u^i v^j] P_n = choose(n-j,i) choose(n-i-1,j).

All subtractions in this display are natural subtraction, including n=0.
Zero cases are retained. The proof factors the two summands into a common
binomial and applies Pascal, with the out-of-range cases proved zero.

On a fixed diagonal i+j=r<n, the P_n coefficients can be written as

    choose(n-r+i,n-r) choose(n-i-1,n-r-1).

The first factor has increasing upper index and the second decreasing upper
index. Each satisfies upper-index binomial log-concavity, and their pointwise
product does too. For r>=n the left endpoint of a consecutive triple is zero.
Thus every constant-total diagonal of P_n is log-concave without restrictions
on n, including zeros. MarkovPellDiagonal0618 proves this inequality directly.

The exponent shear u->xt, v->t sends [u^i v^j] to [t^(i+j)x^i].
MarkovPellShear0618 proves this coefficient transport by polynomial induction.
The actual source quotient at path replicate(n,true) equals the sheared P_(n+1).
This follows from the canonical source core and the existing literal positive
quotient matrices; its row state is exactly (E_n,P_n). Consequently

    [x^i] quotientSlice(replicate(n,true), i+j)
      = choose(n+1-j,i) choose(n-i,j).

This is an exact source identity, not an assumed coefficient formula.
The quotient residual is log-concave for every slice, and inherited interval
support promotes it to CrossLC. For this family a=n+1,b=n+2, the degree is 2a.
Every polygon point has i+j>=a, so every nonzero raw diagonal is in the upper
half where the inherited factorization is multiplication by
(1+x)^(2a-2r). Binomial smoothing transfers residual LC to raw LC. No invalid
inverse-smoothing argument is used for the lower half: it has no polygon points.

The final theorem source_near_one_diagonal0618 quantifies over every actual
source path with b=a+1 and every polygon-guarded consecutive triple in direction
(1,-1). It covers infinitely many diagonals of unbounded degree. It does not
prove the horizontal or vertical directions for this whole family, and does not
prove diagonals for all other rational sources.

## Experiments and rejected strategies

The formula matched 54,858 coefficient checks through n=40. The raw arbitrary
gas-core scan examined every binary core through length 17 and found failures
in all three directions. Its first diagonal example is AAAAAAAAA C A C A
(nine A letters followed by CACA), with coefficients 6,8,11. It is not a source.

A refined exact enumeration of 33 source cores tracked each site's deletion
indicator. Preserving the coordinatewise sum of those indicators across pairs
cannot give the desired injection: for 1/3 and vertical raw coefficients 1,2,3,
the selected fiber has 2 center pairs and 3 endpoint pairs. All three principal
directions have examples of this finer obstruction. Raw pair counts need not
fail when a refined fiber fails. The experiment is refined-pairs.json.

Positive symmetric site weights also fail to preserve LC on a genuine source
core. The 1/4 core AAA with weights 2,1,2 has vertical coefficients 4,4,5.
MarkovSiteObstruction0618 proves the uniform-site source identity and checks
this deformed polynomial's failure. The uniform weights remain the actual
source, so this is not a root refutation. The 21,000 finite weighted tests are
in weighted-source-cores.json.

## Literature used

The [published Markov paper](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html)
was retrieved live; its positive Pell recurrence is consistent with the new
matching representation. The Lean proofs use the pinned source recurrence.

[Leake--Mohammadi Yekta, arXiv:2609.39917v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.39917v1)
proves midpoint log-concavity of finite integer fibers of unimodular systems.
A common affine-fiber model for both raw indices would imply arbitrary-direction
concavity, which the inherited actual-source 1/9 example rules out. This is an
inference about that proposed application, not a claim refuting their theorem.
No external theorem is imported as a Lean axiom. The site-refined test separately
rejects a natural weight-preserving pairing strategy.

[Christoffel words and the strong Fox conjecture](https://arxiv.org/html/2212.04561)
was retrieved after the v3 HTML endpoint failed. It concerns a different
polynomial, and no correspondence to the pinned coefficients is asserted here.
# Right-spine column and horizontal normalization obstruction

Machine-authored live request f6506bc615574382b93e600ac6a368f9. Partial research;
no resolution of the full published conjecture or historical novelty claim.

Let P_a be the exact source numerator at a/(a+1), a>=1. The canonical path
is a-1 right steps. The checked source recurrence is

    P_(a+2)=(u+v+1)(u+v)P_(a+1)-uv P_a.

The same recurrence yields simultaneous exact formulas for columns 0,1,2.
For a>=5 the new formula is

    2[u^2]P_a=v^(a-1)(1+v)^(a-5) R_a(v),
    R_a=16+(32a-16)v+(9a^2+29a-26)v^2
                 +(12a^2+2a-6)v^3+(4a^2-2a)v^4.

The factor 2 clears the coefficient formula uniformly; it is removed again
from the final raw inequality. No factorial or binomial normalization is
used by this positive result. MarkovRightJetsF650 proves the recurrence,
actual low-column computation, and unbounded identity by two-step induction.

Put a=n+5. The residual coefficients are

    16, 32n+144, 9n^2+119n+344, 12n^2+122n+304, 4n^2+38n+90.

They are positive for n>=0. Their three adjacent LC gaps are respectively

    880n^2+7312n+15232,
    81n^4+1758n^3+14721n^2+54576n+74560,
    108n^4+2110n^3+15472n^2+50394n+61456.

The exact real polynomial identities and positivity are checked in Lean.
The finite support is an interval, so the inherited adjacent-to-CrossLC
bridge applies with its support hypothesis discharged. Monomial shifts and
Pascal smoothing preserve this predicate. The resulting theorem covers every
natural j, including zero coefficients. Small a=1,2,3,4 are handled separately
by exact jets and the source outside-polygon-zero theorem.

MarkovRightSourceF650 proves that a source path with b=a+1 consists entirely
of right steps, using the strict lower-endpoint and middle label inequalities.
Thus source_near_one_vertical_two650 covers every source path satisfying
b=a+1, with no denominator bound. It proves only vertical column i=2.

## Obstruction to a stronger horizontal strategy

The exact finite strengthened scan of 307 reduced fractions with b<=31 found
that horizontal binomial normalization does not always preserve LC. The actual
source 12/13 has degree 24, and on row j=14 the coefficients at i=0,1,2 are

    11, 510, 10680.

All three positions are in its polygon. Dividing these by choose(10,i) gives
11,51,712/3, with 51^2=2601 < 7832/3. However the raw inequality is
11*10680=117480 <= 260100=510^2. MarkovHorizontalObstructionF650 proves the
exact coefficients from the universal jets, the source labels, polygon guards,
the strictly reversed normalized inequality and the valid raw inequality.
This is a proof-strategy obstruction, not a refutation of Conjecture 6.3.

The same finite scan found both signs among neighboring coefficient-matrix
minors; neither uniform TP2 sign is an available general invariant. No failure
of the tested positive-slope adjacent inequality was found. That observation
is finite only and is not an additional proved source direction.

# Horizontal jet and scope of the experiments

Machine-authored research, 2026-10-14. Full Conjecture 6.3 remains open.

For a raw A--core--B word, put n=core.length and m=core.count(B).
At v=0 the generators are scalar multiples of the same rank-one matrix.
If (p,q) is the first row after A and the core processed so far, then

* p(0)=0 and q(0)=u^m(1+u)^n;
* (u+1)[p'(0)+(u+1)q'(0)]
  =q(0)[u+1+nu+m(u+3)].

Here the derivatives mean first coefficients, so no factorial or normalization
enters. MarkovRowJetB46 proves the invariant over every commutative ring.
Multiplication by the final B gives

    (u+1)[v]P = u^(m+1)(u+1)^n[(3m+2)+(n+m+2)u].

The cancellation for n>=1 is in the integral polynomial ring; n=0 gives 2u
directly. MarkovHorizontalB46 connects the word to every actual source path
and proves ((swap P).coeff j).coeff i=coeff P i j. The resulting label form is

    [v]P_(a/b) = u^a(1+u)^(b-3)[(3a-1)+(a+b-1)u], b>=3.

MarkovHorizontalLCB46 proves the zero-extended CrossLC predicate and literal
integer raw horizontal inequality on j=1, for every path and every natural i.
The first-row source result is known in published Theorem 6.6; this work is
a checked exact bridge and no historical novelty is claimed.

MarkovVerticalBoundaryB46 uses the triangular u=0 specialization to prove
[u^0]P=v^b(v+1)^(a-1), and its raw vertical coefficient inequality for every
path and natural j. This is likewise a boundary result, not the interior goal.

The actual source at 2/5, path LR, has horizontal row j=2 equal to
u^2(14+28u+15u^2). Its quadratic factor has discriminant -56 and is positive
at every real argument; the raw coefficients satisfy 14*15<=28^2. Thus a
real-rootedness requirement is stronger than horizontal raw LC. The Lean
example supplies the exact source identity and algebraic certificates.
source_horizontal_nonreal_zero46 additionally constructs
z=(-14+i sqrt(14))/15 and proves its imaginary part nonzero and its evaluation
in the actual integer source row, mapped to complex numbers, equal to zero.
See the final validation manifest for its build/replay receipts.

## Source formula discrepancy, separate from the conjecture

The live [publisher text](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html)
was retrieved on 2026-10-14. Its Theorem 4.2 displays

    A_(i,1)=(3a-1) choose(b-2,i-a)+(b-2) choose(b-3,i-a-1).

At a=2,b=3,i=3 this is 6. The actual recurrence gives 4; the explicit
source polynomial displayed in section 3 also gives 4. Theorem 4.1 instead
has the second prefactor b-2a, which gives 4 and agrees with the checked
linear factor above. printed_row_formula_mismatch46 proves the exact
recurrence value and displayed numeric value. This does not refute 6.3.
No protected root or paper statement has been silently altered.

## Finite experiments and revisable guidance

word-directions-16.json checks 32,767 raw A--core--B words of length <=16.
No horizontal failure occurred, whereas 2,625 words failed vertically and
5,688 diagonally. This motivates the unproved broader horizontal-only claim.
It does not justify enlarging the word family for the full root. Under B->AC,
these expanded words have no consecutive C letters; a future horizontal
argument might exploit that restriction. This is advice, not a proved lemma.

The exact rational Sturm routine found the same nonreal source horizontal
example at 2/5 when fractions were ordered by denominator. Earlier exploratory
output found a larger example first; both remain preserved. No numerical
root routine or Sturm output is a Lean theorem.

Circularly balanced, reduced words with the prescribed A/B endpoints can
also fail unrestricted diagonal LC: ABBABABABABAB, counts 7/13, has coefficients
2,6,20 at (5,3),(6,2),(7,1). However (5,3) is outside the canonical 7/13
polygon, and the actual source coefficients are 0,4,20. This is only an
